summary: Evaluated logistic regression and random forest on 320 unique customers with an explicit churn target; stratified holdout test size was 80 (25.0%). Positive class: 'Churn'. Best holdout ROC AUC: 0.771 (Logistic Regression).

Evaluated logistic regression and random forest on 320 unique customers with an explicit churn target; stratified holdout test size was 80 (25.0%). Positive class: 'Churn'. Best holdout ROC AUC: 0.771 (Logistic Regression).
Highest held-out ROC AUC: 0.771 for Logistic Regression; this ranks discrimination on this sample, not real-world usefulness by itself.
Logistic Regression positive-class recall: 70.0%; proportion of observed positive cases detected in the holdout at the tested threshold.
Random Forest positive-class recall: 45.0%; proportion of observed positive cases detected in the holdout at the tested threshold.

interpretation.business_implications: The model comparison estimates how well selected pre-outcome customer attributes separate the explicitly defined churn class from the other observed class on a held-out sample. Use recall/precision and the costs of missed churn versus unnecessary outreach to choose an operating threshold; the default 0.5 threshold is not necessarily appropriate.
interpretation.root_cause_assessment: The output is descriptive unless the method explicitly reports a validated inferential or predictive result. Any proposed explanation of why the pattern occurred is a hypothesis to investigate, not a proven cause.
recommendations: Compare ROC AUC, balanced accuracy, recall and precision against a simple baseline and the cost of each error before selecting a model.
Review the holdout confusion matrix and the top features for data leakage, stability and business plausibility.
Before deployment, validate on a later time period, calibrate risk scores if probability estimates are required, and pilot a human-reviewed retention queue.

Recall and precision for the defined churn class

limitations: This is an exploratory random holdout result, not a calibrated production probability or causal retention effect. Results can be optimistic if selected features contain post-outcome information or if a random split leaks time patterns.

Exploratory holdout estimates, not a validated production churn model or calibrated probability of churn. Selected predictors are aggregated to customer level (numeric mean; categorical mode); this is defensible only if all predictors precede the churn window. Use time-based validation for deployment, check leakage, drift, calibration, subgroup performance and intervention capacity. Precision/recall depend on the selected positive class and threshold; a high score does not prove a customer will churn.
interpretation.evidence_status: Computed result + conservative rule-based interpretation; causal claims not inferred.
